description: Sync customers, invoices, payments, bills and attachments from one QuickBooks Online company. Invoices and payments link to their customer, and attached files are read so their text is searchable.
opening: Sync customers, invoices, payments, bills and attachments from one QuickBooks Online company. Each record is one document. Invoices and payments link to their customer. Each attachment is its own document, linked to the records it is attached to, and its file is read so its text is searchable.

QuickBooks permissions are not imported, so every synced record is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Every sync reads all records of each selected type again, which is slow for companies with many invoices. Records deleted in QuickBooks stay in HydraDB. Vendors, items and accounts are not their own documents.

notes: Each record type you select is its own resource, so you can set an access rule on one type, such as Invoices, and not on the others.

connect.auth: QuickBooks uses the client id and client secret of an Intuit developer app, with a refresh token and the company id of the company you connect.

credentials.name: client_id
credentials.text: The client id of your Intuit developer app, from its Keys & credentials page.

credentials.name: client_secret
credentials.text: The client secret of the same app.

credentials.name: refresh_token
credentials.text: An OAuth refresh token for the company.

credentials.name: realmId
credentials.text: The QuickBooks company id that the refresh token belongs to.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: Leave it empty. HydraDB obtains access tokens itself.

connect.credentials_note: Intuit replaces the refresh token from time to time. HydraDB stores each new refresh token itself.

steps.title: Create an Intuit app
steps.text: In the Intuit developer portal, create an app and copy its client id and client secret.

steps.title: Get a refresh token and company id
steps.text: Get a refresh token for the company you want to connect, and that company's id. The Intuit OAuth Playground is one place to get both.

steps.title: Select record types
steps.text: HydraDB lists five record types: Customers, Invoices, Payments, Bills and Attachments. Select the ones to sync. Each selected type is synced on its own.

connect.account: One connector reads one QuickBooks Online company.

sync.first_sync: Reads every record of each selected type, whatever its date. `lookback_days` does not narrow it.
sync.changes: Every sync reads every record of each selected type again.
sync.edits: A changed record replaces its document.
sync.deletes: Deleted records are not removed. A record deleted in QuickBooks stays searchable in HydraDB.

shared_attributes.name: updated_at
shared_attributes.text: When the record was last updated in QuickBooks. It is the result date, and it appears in the text.

shared_attributes.name: created_at
shared_attributes.text: When the record was created in QuickBooks. It is the result date only when there is no update time. Searchable on customers. Not searchable on other record types.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.quickbooks_id
shared_attributes.text: The record's QuickBooks Id, without its record type. Finds a record by its Id. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's records. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: Other QuickBooks fields
shared_attributes.text: Every other field QuickBooks returns for the record. Kept for inspection only. A query does not match them and cannot filter on them.

documents.name: Customers
documents.title: The customer's display name. Otherwise the fully qualified name, the company name, or the first and last name.
documents.text: Contact details: the display name, first and last name, email, phone numbers, website, whether the customer is a person or an organization, the company or parent customer name, and the created and updated times. Then the customer's QuickBooks notes, followed by `Name`, `Company`, `Email`, `Phone` and `Balance` lines. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the customer was last updated, or created when there is no update time.
documents.files: Files attached to a customer arrive as separate attachment documents linked to it.

attributes.name: display_name
attributes.text: The customer's display name. It forms the title and names the customer in the graph.

attributes.name: first_name
attributes.text: The customer's given name. Helps form the person's name when there is no display name.

attributes.name: last_name
attributes.text: The customer's family name. Helps form the person's name when there is no display name.

attributes.name: email
attributes.text: The customer's primary email. Identifies a person customer in the graph.

attributes.name: entity_type
attributes.text: Organization when the customer has a company name, otherwise person. Decides whether the graph records the customer as a person or as an organization.

attributes.name: provider_user_id
attributes.text: The customer's QuickBooks Id, for person customers only. Empty for organizations. Identifies the person in the graph.

attributes.name: phones
attributes.text: The primary, mobile, alternate and fax numbers, each once. Phone numbers do not identify the customer in the graph.

attributes.name: url
attributes.text: The customer's website. It is part of the text, not a link back to QuickBooks.

attributes.name: organization_name
attributes.text: The company name for an organization, or the parent customer's name for a person.

attributes.name: organization_id
attributes.text: For a person, the parent customer's id. Links the person to that parent customer. Empty for organizations.

attributes.name: emails
attributes.text: An empty list. Secondary email addresses are not kept.

documents.name: Invoices
documents.title: `Invoice <number> - <customer>`.
documents.text: The customer memo, then `Customer`, `Total`, `Balance`, `Invoice date`, `Due date`, `Line items` and `Note` lines, and the update time. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the invoice was last updated, or created when there is no update time.
documents.files: Files attached to an invoice arrive as separate attachment documents linked to it.

attributes.name: CustomerRef
attributes.text: The customer the invoice belongs to. Its id links the invoice to the customer's document. Its name is in the title and the `Customer` line. The id itself is not searchable.

attributes.name: DocNumber
attributes.text: The invoice number, in the title.

attributes.name: Line items
attributes.text: Each line's description with its item or account name, written into the `Line items` line. Other line details are not searchable.

documents.name: Payments
documents.title: `Payment <reference> - <customer>`.
documents.text: The private note, then `Customer`, `Total`, `Payment date` and `Reference` lines, and the update time. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the payment was last updated, or created when there is no update time.
documents.files: Files attached to a payment arrive as separate attachment documents linked to it.

attributes.name: CustomerRef
attributes.text: The customer who paid. Its id links the payment to the customer's document. Its name is in the title and the `Customer` line. The id itself is not searchable.

attributes.name: PaymentRefNum
attributes.text: The payment reference, in the title and the `Reference` line.

documents.name: Bills
documents.title: `Bill <number> - <vendor>`.
documents.text: The private note, then `Vendor`, `Total`, `Balance`, `Bill date`, `Due date` and `Line items` lines, and the update time. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the bill was last updated, or created when there is no update time.
documents.files: Files attached to a bill arrive as separate attachment documents linked to it.

attributes.name: VendorRef
attributes.text: The vendor's name, in the title and the `Vendor` line. Vendors are not their own documents, so a bill is not linked to a vendor.

attributes.name: DocNumber
attributes.text: The bill number, in the title.

attributes.name: Line items
attributes.text: Each line's description with its item or account name, written into the `Line items` line. Other line details are not searchable.

documents.name: Attachments
documents.one_document: One attachment: a file or a note.
documents.title: The file name.
documents.text: When the file's text is read, that text is the document's text. Otherwise, the attachment note, then `File name`, `Content type` and `File size` lines. The title and the update time are searchable either way.
documents.date: When the attachment was last updated, or created when there is no update time.
documents.files: The file is downloaded and its text is read. A file larger than 50 MiB is not downloaded, and only its note and file details are searchable.

attributes.name: File text
attributes.text: The text read from the file, such as a PDF attached to an invoice.

attributes.name: Note
attributes.text: The attachment note. Searchable only when the file's text was not read. Read file text takes its place.

attributes.name: ContentType, Size
attributes.text: The file's media type and size. Searchable only when the file's text was not read. Otherwise kept for inspection.

attributes.name: AttachableRef
attributes.text: Every QuickBooks record the file is attached to. Links the attachment to each of those records. Not searchable.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The first record the file is attached to. The graph places the attachment under that record. Not searchable, and not a query filter.

example_searches: What is the outstanding balance on invoices for Acme Corp?
What does the contract PDF attached to invoice 1042 say?
Which bills from Office Depot still have a balance?

connections: An attachment to every record it is attached to, and under the first of them.
A person customer to its parent customer, when it has one.
Bills are not linked to a vendor.
people: Each customer: as a person, or as an organization when it has a company name.
For a person customer with a parent customer, the parent as their organization.
Vendors are not attached as people or organizations. They appear in bill text only.
graph.from_text: Customer notes, invoice memos, payment and bill notes, line items and attachment text.

not_synced: Record types you did not select.
Vendors, items, accounts, estimates, sales receipts, credit memos, journal entries and other QuickBooks record types. Vendors, items and accounts appear only as names in bills and line items.
QuickBooks reports, such as profit and loss or the balance sheet.
Deletions: records deleted in QuickBooks stay in HydraDB.
The text of files larger than 50 MiB.
